environment: Windows 11, CR-M8bc and CR-M8bcf2 critics; jjv editorial boundaries write
symptom: (a) A draft run left a stale boundaries.json in place as if it were final. (b) A crash between writing boundaries.json and writing its receipt left the folder unreadable or read as a legacy folder.
root_cause: Measured by CR-M8bc: draft writes could touch the current files, and the publish order had no marker, so a crash between boundaries.json and boundaries.current.json was indistinguishable from an old folder. CR-M8bcf2 found the same window at the receipt-to-swap-log step. Current code: engine/editorial/boundaries_write.py:160-162 (a draft never touches boundaries.json or the receipt; it reports current_is_stale), engine/editorial/boundaries_current.py:68-80 (marker -> boundaries.json -> receipt, then the marker is removed), :103-112 (refuse when boundaries.json does not match its receipt).
root_cause_status: measured (CR-M8bc and CR-M8bcf2 findings; M8b(c)-f2 root accepted 2026-10-29 ~00:30). Current sha256 engine/editorial/boundaries_current.py 4b54987f17fc1984880172fc2aab9e5e1210f7cbd7256a1763788d0725c9874b, engine/editorial/boundaries_write.py be50090fbcf487359ee226a0a73bfb0a4b5eeaa9a29af3b5e33ba2394df03c3d
fix_or_workaround: Write order is marker -> boundaries.json -> boundaries.current.json (receipt) -> marker removed. The marker carries the target version and sha, so an interrupted publish is recognised and completed by an identical retry. Drafts go to versions/boundaries-draft-vNNN.json and report staleness; they never replace the final files. Accepted: M8b(c)-f2 boundaries.current receipt (root re-run).
prevention: Rule to keep: a draft never writes the final file or its receipt. Any multi-file publish writes a marker first, and the reader treats a marker as 'interrupted', never as legacy. Test every crash point between the files, not only the happy path.
